verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Gondal groundnut/cottonseed millers with stock-and-receivables control; avoid vanaspati refiners and unhedged oil traders until raw-material cover and buyer concentration are verified.
title: Gondal Edible Oils & Vanaspati: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Gondal's oil units crush groundnut and cottonseed and press cake; the Rajkot cluster also runs solvent extraction and vanaspati plants [3]. Cash comes from selling oil and cake, so the miller's real exposure is the gap between seed bought at harvest and oil sold weeks later. **The business is a spread business, not a brand business** — CARA notes PBILDT margins of 1.47% to 3.32% for a vanaspati peer on low value addition and fragmented competition [9]. When a proposal lands, check the seed-to-oil yield and the cake realisation separately; if the borrower cannot show both, ask for the crushing register. ## Where value and cash sit
Value sits in the seed inventory and in the cake, not in the refined oil. ICRA flags raw-material price volatility as a key risk for edible oil companies [10]. **Working capital is the loan, and inventory is the collateral that moves.** So take stock statements monthly and revalue at the lower of cost or the mandi price that month; if cover falls below the sanctioned drawing power, ask for the sale invoices before releasing further limits. Capex is modest — a solvent plant or refinery is a one-time block — so treat any large capex request as a separate term-loan decision, not a working-capital top-up. ## What has changed now
Gujarat GST collections are running +11.9% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D], a genuine local tailwind. But India-wide exports are -26.0% Apr-to-date in USD [D] and bank credit is +45.5% YoY against output +5.1% [D]. **Credit is growing far faster than output, so the risk is borrowed stock, not demand.** Peer AWL Agri shows revenue +22% but EBIT -13% and PAT -21% in Q2FY26 [4]; by Q4FY26 revenue rose 18% with 14% volume growth and EBITDA +40% [5][6]. Read that as: volumes are fine, margins are the swing factor. Local Gondal news is about chilli arrivals and groundnut support-price buying at Rs 1,462 per maund [1], not about oil mills — the city-specific oil evidence is thin, so lean on first principles and peers. ## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
Pursue established groundnut and cottonseed crushers in Gondal and Rajkot with their own cake buyers and a named oil buyer [3]. Avoid pure traders and new vanaspati units with no crushing base. **Structure as a cash-credit limit against paid stock and receivables, with a 25% margin and monthly stock statements.** Take the seed purchase register, the sales ledger and GST returns every month; if receivables days stretch beyond the agreed limit, convert the excess to a demand loan. - Seed price vs oil price (weekly): if the crush spread turns negative for two weeks, ask for the hedge or forward-sale contract. - Buyer concentration (quarterly): if one buyer exceeds 40% of sales, ask for the contract and payment history. - GST filing (monthly): if returns lag two months, freeze limits until filed.
